items.title: Ex-UiTM Holdings CEO charged with CBT over RM37.37m meant for Pahang solar project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — A former group chief executive officer of UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd was charged today with criminal breach of trust involving RM37.37 million earmarked for a large-scale solar power project in Pahang. Azlizan Fadzil, 53, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him before Sessions Court judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin, the New Straits Times (NST) reported. According to the charge, Azlizan was entrusted in his capacity as chief executive officer with RM37,374,612.68 intended for investment in a 50-megawatt large-scale solar photovoltaic power generation project in Gambang.

items.title: Two teenage sisters reported missing after leaving home
items.summary: AMPANG JAYA: Two teenage sisters have been reported missing after leaving their home in Lembah Jaya Utara here separately on Sep 26 and Sep 27. The two, Syazana Qurratu Aini Zulhazmi, 17, and her younger sister, Nur Qistina Fhatanah, 16, were reported missing after they failed to return home. Ampang Jaya district police chief, Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid, said Syazana Qurratu Aini had initially gone out with a friend for a meal at a nearby area at 8pm on Sep 26.

items.title: Supply chain resilience tops agenda as Singapore DPM Gan Kim Yong visits Malaysia
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 1 — Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong arrived in Malaysia today for a one-day working visit, with strengthening economic ties and supply chain resilience between the two countries at the top of the agenda. Gan, who is also Singapore trade and industry minister, was warmly welcomed by Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) Deputy Secretary-General (Investment and Management) R. Jaya Singam. During the visit, Gan is scheduled to meet Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and attend a business luncheon with the Malaysia-Singapore Business Council in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Ex-UiTM Holdings CEO charged with CBT involving RM37.37 mil [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UHSB) group chief executive officer Azlizan Fadzil was charged at the Sessions Court here today with criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM37.37 million meant for a large-scale solar power project in Gambang, Pahang. Azlizan, 53, pleaded not guilty to the charge after it was read out before Sessions Court judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. According to the charge, Azlizan, who was then the company's chief executive officer, was entrusted with RM37,374,612.68 for the investment of a 50-megawatt (MW) large-scale solar photovoltaic power generation project in Gambang.

items.title: Malaysia to hand over 292 Malbatt assets to Lebanese Armed Forces
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will hand over 292 Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) assets in Lebanon, worth an estimated US$10 million, to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) as part of the withdrawal process. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the assets, including vehicles and various equipment, would be handed over in stages until January 2027. The assets were symbolically handed over by Joint Forces Commander Lieutenant-General Datuk Seri Tengku Muhammad Fauzi Tengku Ibrahim to LAF representative Brigadier-General Bassem Saad.

items.title: Guardiola pledges loyalty to Man City as punishment looms over financial rule breach scandal
items.summary: MANCHESTER, Oct 1 — Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola threw his weight behind the club on Wednesday after a bombshell verdict on Premier League financial rule breaches plunged their future into serious doubt. Premier League chief executive Richard Masters described the disciplinary case and the decision by an independent commission as the “most significant in Premier League history”. He said City “systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade”, adding that the league was committed to a swift resolution.

items.title: AI, intelligence-led probes and fair enforcement: MACC’s five priorities at 59
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Nearly six decades into its fight against corruption, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) continues to strengthen its strategies to ensure enforcement, prevention and integrity remain at the heart of its work. As the agency marks its 59th anniversary today, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman outlined five leadership priorities to guide his administration: uncompromising integrity, fair and equitable enforcement, proactive prevention, adopting technology, and transparency and public trust. “For MACC, firm enforcement does not mean disregarding the principles of justice.

items.title: Razali Idris hints at leaving Bersatu for 'new platform'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Terengganu Bersatu chief Datuk Razali Idris has hinted at leaving the party, saying he would move forward on a "new platform". "Ten years as a Bersatu leader ends today. Last month, Razali said he remained a Bersatu member despite relinquishing his position as the party's Terengganu chief.

items.title: Three homes hit by mudslide after heavy rain in Sungai Petani
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 1 — Three houses in Kampung Serukam here were affected by a mudslide following heavy rain yesterday afternoon. The incident is believed to have occurred after heavy rain began at about 12.30pm, causing a collapse at a nearby housing project site, before water and mud flowed into residents’ homes. Meanwhile, Scientex SP Astana project site supervisor Mohd Haniff Ramli said three houses were affected in the incident, including two located within the project site.

items.title: California roller coaster permanently shut after brain injury claims
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: A popular California roller coaster is being permanently shut down after dozens of people claimed to have suffered brain damage while riding it. But it has also sparked a rash of legal complaints, including from two women whose families say they were seriously injured in July on the ride in Valencia, just north of Los Angeles. Less than a week later, Naomi Greer-Wilkinson of Los Angeles, 25, lost consciousness after riding X2 and underwent emergency brain surgery, CNN reported.

items.title: SpaceX donates 50 Starlink kits to Malaysia for disaster preparedness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — United States Aerospace Company, SpaceX, yesterday donated 50 units of Starlink kits to Malaysia to support the country’s disaster preparedness, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said the contribution was presented by a SpaceX delegation that made a courtesy call on him at the Perdana Putra Building in Putrajaya, which was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Anwar said the meeting, among other things, discussed efforts to strengthen strategic cooperation through Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by the company, with a specific focus on expanding network access to residents in rural areas.

items.title: Gig economy should be temporary income source, says Economy Minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The gig economy should be viewed as a temporary source of income rather than a comprehensive solution to the challenges of jobs and wages, says Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. However, prolonged reliance on such work did not necessarily offer income stability, opportunities to develop skills or clearer career progression, he said. He said the country's real challenge was to create more quality jobs that enabled workers to improve their skills and income over time.

items.title: RM6,000 work permit deal leads to arrest of alleged fake Immigration officer
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 1 — The Melaka Immigration Department (JIM) has arrested a housewife suspected of impersonating a senior immigration officer and offering services to process work pass applications for foreigners. Melaka Immigration director Anirwan Fauzee Mohd Aini said the woman, in her 50s, was detained in a raid under Op Serkap at a cafe in Taman Malim Jaya here at about 6 pm yesterday. The items seized included a set of black uniform with accessories, a pair of senior immigration officer rank insignia, a pair of JIM collar badges, a JIM integrity badge, two grey headscarves, two black T-shirts bearing the JIM logo and a forged JIM identification card.

items.title: FTC launches AI safety probe into Anthropic, OpenAI
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Federal Trade Commission has launched a broad investigation into artificial intelligence safety practices at Anthropic and OpenAI, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday. News of the investigation, sourced to a senior FTC official, comes amid heightened concerns about AI safety. AI giants Anthropic and OpenAI have reported instances of their systems escaping into the wild, including an incident where OpenAI agents breached Hugging Face, another AI company.

items.title: Zulkifli: Tabung Haji RCI follow-up must be firm and comprehensive
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan is focusing on ensuring firm and comprehensive follow-up actions are taken on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) after appearing before the Parliamentary Public Accounts Committee (PAC). “The main focus at this juncture is to ensure that follow-up actions on the TH RCI Report are completed in a firm and comprehensive manner,” he said in a Facebook post. Zulkifli said he had reviewed all relevant documents, including the Tabung Haji Act and the RCI Report, before attending the more than two-hour session.

items.title: Parliamentary Services Act 2025 takes effect today
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Parliamentary Services Act 2025 (Act 869) and related amendments to the Federal Constitution take effect today, marking a significant milestone in efforts to strengthen Parliament's institutional autonomy. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the enactment of Act 869 was a significant achievement for the Madani government's institutional reform agenda and a historic milestone for the Malaysian Parliament. She said this came 34 years after the Parliamentary Services Act 1963 (Act 394) was repealed under the Constitution (Amendment) Act 1992 (Act A837), effective Nov 20, 1992.

items.title: Zulkifli condemns Al-Aqsa incursions, backs call for international action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The incursion by illegal Israeli settlers into the Al-Aqsa Mosque Complex and the Ibrahimi Mosque in Palestine constitutes a clear violation of international law, asserted the Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Zulkifli Hasan. He noted that the Al-Aqsa Mosque as the first ‘Qibla’ (direction of prayer) for Muslims represents a red line that must be defended by the entire Muslim community without compromise. “The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) fully supports the firm stance taken by Wisma Putra and calls upon the international community to take appropriate action in response to the Zionist regime’s insolence and to demand accountability,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.

items.title: Google withholds new AI model from public over safety fears
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Google on Wednesday said it would withhold its most powerful artificial intelligence model from the public for now, releasing Gemini 4 Argon only to a vetted group of cybersecurity experts to avoid misuse by hackers. "Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach," wrote Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google's chief AI architect, in a blog post announcing the model. Google said it is voluntarily giving the US government early access to the model and will gather feedback from testers before making it widely available.

items.title: Half of p-hailing riders rely on gig work full-time, survey finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: About half of more than 5,000 p-hailing riders surveyed nationwide rely on gig work as a full-time job. As such, Haris said the association disagreed with the perception that gig work in Malaysia was only suitable as a temporary job. Gig workers nationwide are estimated to number 1.12 million, including about 600,000 p-hailing riders.

items.title: Tourist dies after losing consciousness during Tioman scuba dive
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 1 — A 55-year-old Afghan man died while taking part in a Discovery Scuba Diving (DSD) activity in the waters off Kampung Salang, Pulau Tioman, Rompin, yesterday. Rompin police chief Supt Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the victim, Mohammed Seyar Musazay, who was residing in California, United States, was confirmed dead at about 12.40pm after being taken to the Kampung Tekek Health Clinic. “At about 11am, the victim, his daughter and a scuba instructor went out to take part in the DSD activity.

items.title: At Dr Hasmah’s grave, Malaysians reflect on a life that touched generations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Three days after the demise of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, her resting place at Pusara Negara continues to see a steady stream of visitors, offering prayers and expressions of gratitude. For several medical officers from the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health, the visit held special significance, as they had grown up during the era of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Tun Dr Siti Hasmah. “I was born and raised during the era of Tun (Dr) M and (Tun Dr) Siti Hasmah.

items.title: Esscom focuses on protecting vulnerable groups from exploitation
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) is stepping up efforts to protect undocumented and stateless communities from exploitation amid cross-border security threats. Its commander Datuk Victor Sanjos said the lack of valid identification documents, limited access to formal employment, socioeconomic factors and the location of some communities in island and coastal areas could create conditions that might be exploited by irresponsible parties. Victor said Esscom's approach also took into account threats including cross-border crime, syndicate activities and exploitation.

items.title: Malaysia restores parliamentary service after 34 years as new law takes effect
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Parliamentary Services Act 2025 (Act 869) and related amendments to the Federal Constitution take effect today. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Act’s enactment is a significant achievement for the Madani Government’s institutional reform agenda and a historic milestone for the Malaysian Parliament, 34 years after the Parliamentary Services Act 1963 (Act 394) was repealed under the Constitution (Amendment) Act 1992 (Act A837), effective Nov 20, 1992. She said the Madani Government also expressed its gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting consent to set Oct 1, 2026, as the date on which Act 869 and related amendments to the Federal Constitution would come into force.

items.title: Kedah RTD issues 4,447 summonses in foreign driver crackdown
items.summary: ALOR STAR: The Kedah Road Transport Department (RTD) issued 4,447 summonses to foreign drivers during an operation targeting foreign drivers conducted from June 17 until yesterday. Kedah RTD director Stien Van Lutam said the summonses were issued for various offences under relevant laws. Main offences detected throughout the operation included driving without a valid driving licence, expired Motor Vehicle Licences (LKM) or road tax, and driving without valid insurance coverage.

items.title: Ab Rauf: Umno divisions to submit three names for each state seat
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Melaka Umno will examine the list of candidates submitted by its divisions, as well as MCA and MIC, ahead of the state election. State Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said all Umno leaders have been asked to submit at least three potential candidates for each state seat for review. Also present were state Umno Liaison Committee deputy chairman Datuk Rais Yasin and all division chiefs, including Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, who is also Jasin Umno division chief.

items.title: MACC urges tighter governance at Felda and subsidiaries over two projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has proposed governance improvements to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and two of its subsidiaries to strengthen the management of two projects under the agency. In a statement yesterday, MACC said the subsidiaries involved were FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd (FIC Supplies) and FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM). “MACC BPT also recommended that Felda strengthen its procurement and transaction management procedures by establishing specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for procurement methods involving request for proposal (RFP) and variation orders,” the statement said.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain forecast for Terengganu, Sarawak until 9am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in parts of Terengganu and Sarawak until 9am today. In a statement this morning, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Kemaman in Terengganu. In Sarawak, the areas affected are Sri Aman, Samarahan (Sebuyau), Betong, Kapit (Song), Sarikei, Mukah and Bintulu.

items.title: Trump's AI chatbot pulls back after debunking his political claims
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump unveiled what he called a "damn good" AI chatbot, but it quickly drew attention for contradicting some of his contentious political claims. The chatbot soon began contradicting Trump on controversial subjects such as the 2020 presidential election, which he wrongly claims to have won, and the Jan 6, 2021 insurrection that saw a violent mob attacking the US Capitol. Democratic lawmakers quickly promoted the chatbot's responses about the election.

items.title: Budget 2027 to consider cost pressures on small businesses, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The government will study the cost pressures in procurement and operations faced by small enterprises following the global supply crisis when formulating Budget 2027, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the matter was among those raised during the Budget 2027 engagement session with representatives of associations and Bumiputera contractor companies held at Perdana Putra, Putrajaya, yesterday. He said all views and suggestions put forward during the session have been taken into account to be properly examined in the preparation of the budget.

items.title: F1 weekend drives 160pc surge in accommodation searches for KL and Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia is seeing a surge in travel interest ahead of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit, with accommodation searches for Kuala Lumpur, Sepang and surrounding areas jumping more than 160 per cent year-on-year for the October 2 to 4 race weekend. “Travel today is increasingly shaped by experiences. Within the surrounding areas, Kuala Lumpur accounted for more than 60 per cent of searches, followed by Sepang at nearly 25 per cent, alongside Petaling and Hulu Langat.

items.title: Pahang fitness icon chases another record with 9,000-rep challenge on Nov 1
items.summary: LIPIS: Pahang-born fitness instructor K. Jey Prabakaran Thevar, who set a world record with an 18-hour endurance workout in June, is raising the bar with another gruelling challenge. He previously secured a place in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBOR) for completing the highest number of jumping jacks, leg extensions and squats within 48 hours in Kuala Lipis last year. Jey Prabakaran said that after completing 3,000 repetitions of each exercise during last year's National Sports Day celebration to secure the MBOR title, he was now aiming to complete the same number of repetitions in each exercise within five hours for the Asian record attempt.

items.title: Meeting with 25 Negeri Sembilan assemblymen did not discuss MB’s royal audience, says Jalaluddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — A special meeting with 25 Negeri Sembilan state assemblymen last night did not discuss Tuesday’s audience between Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, said state Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias. He said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had urged the assemblymen not to be affected by current developments and to continue prioritising service to the people following the political situation in the state. He said the meeting was also attended by Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against major currencies, lower versus greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against a basket of major currencies, but slightly lower against the US dollar on Thursday, weighed by strong US economic data that supported the greenback. At 8am, the ringgit edged down to 4.0790/0860 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0785/0820. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam said the US final gross domestic product (GDP) for the second quarter of 2026 came in at 2.2 per cent, above the consensus estimate of 1.5 per cent.

items.title: 10 areas record unhealthy air quality at 7am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas recorded unhealthy air quality readings as of 7am today, according to the Air Pollutant Index (API). Based on readings from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Johan Setia recorded the highest API reading at 157, followed by Shah Alam (156) and Nilai (153). Meanwhile, 54 locations recorded moderate API readings, while four others recorded good readings.

items.title: Flydubai cockpit attack prompts Israel to tighten pilot security checks
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel is set to ramp up security checks on pilots flying into the country, a spokesperson for the prime minister's office said, after it said a co-pilot on a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv had stabbed the pilot and attempted to crash the plane. The Dubai state-owned airline warned against "premature speculation" and said much remained unclear. Saudi authorities have arrested and interrogated the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 from the United Arab Emirates to Israel that was carrying 174 people, almost all Israelis, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.

items.title: Meta given until Oct 2 to respond over WhatsApp account issues, says MCMC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is demanding a comprehensive explanation from Meta regarding issues involving WhatsApp accounts that have been suspended, rendered inaccessible, or accessed without authorisation. “Meta has requested until October 2 to provide feedback regarding the matter. Earlier yesterday, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he had instructed MCMC to issue a statement clarifying Meta’s response regarding the issues of hacking and the deactivation of WhatsApp accounts.

items.title: BoJ debated need for more rate hikes at September meeting, summary shows
items.summary: TOKYO: Some Bank of Japan (BoJ) policymakers saw the need to accelerate the pace of interest rate hikes or bring them closer to the central bank's "goal" soon, a summary of opinions at its September meeting showed on Thursday. "If signs of an upward deviation in prices are observed, the bank will need to accelerate the pace of rate hikes," one member was quoted as saying. At the September meeting, the BoJ raised interest rates to a 31-year high with its governor signalling the central bank has entered a new phase focused on preventing inflation from overshooting its target, opening the door to further rate hikes.

items.title: Etihad Airways seeks legal advice after Premier League's Man City findings
items.summary: MANCHESTER: Abu Dhabi-based airline Etihad Airways said on Wednesday it was seeking legal advice on its options after criticising the Premier League's handling of an independent commission's findings against Manchester City. Etihad, City's principal sponsor since 2009, said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication" that it was involved in improper commercial arrangements. A Premier League spokesperson said on Wednesday they would not be commenting on the Etihad statement.

items.title: Netanyahu hails Indian pilot who saved 174 aboard flydubai jet
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hailed Indian pilot Smit Machchhar for saving passengers after he was stabbed by his colleague in an alleged attempt to crash a flydubai plane on Wednesday. Passengers on the flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after customers and crew foiled the co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said. "He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals," Netanyahu said in a post on X.

items.title: Five pillars to steer MACC as it enters sixth decade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Integrity without compromise, fair enforcement, proactive prevention, greater use of technology and public trust will form the five pillars steering the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) as it approaches six decades in the fight against graft. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the five pillars would guide the commission's administration and direction as corruption becomes increasingly complex and evolves alongside technology. Speaking in an interview in conjunction with MACC's 59th anniversary recently, Halim said the commission could not afford to remain static.

items.title: Investing according to human behaviour
items.summary: Templeton's message goes beyond market timing. Economic conditions may be weak, corporate profits may have fallen, unemployment may be high and financial news may be dominated by bad headlines. Investors become convinced that the future will remain bleak.

items.title: Former EPF chief calls for review of retirement age
items.summary: Shahril, who is now Axiata Group Bhd chairman, said longer life expectancy and Malaysians' willingness to remain economically active could justify more flexible working arrangements beyond 60, including part-time work. Shahril said flexible working arrangements could help older Malaysians remain economically active. "The retirement age should be formally amended under the Minimum Retirement Age Act 2012.

items.title: UK PM Burnham: 'Really concerned' if Man City owners sell club
items.summary: MANCHESTER: Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's Abu Dhabi owners decided to sell the club after they were found guilty of serious breaches of financial rules. Burnham praised the ownership group led by Sheikh Mansour for its investment in Manchester since taking over the club in 2008. City have denied wrongdoing and said they will appeal.

items.title: Melaka battle lines remain fluid as parties struggle with electoral pacts
items.summary: Syaza said Pas appeared relatively comfortable with either cooperating with BN or contesting independently, while BN leaders in Melaka had from the outset appeared inclined towards going solo. She said PH, meanwhile, may see value in working with Bersatu, but Bersatu could calculate that it had little to lose by contesting on its own. "If BN, PH, Bersatu and Pas eventually move separately, the Melaka election could become a highly fragmented multi-cornered contest.

items.title: Midnight boats fuel fear among islanders in Tumpat [WATCH]
items.summary: TUMPAT: Residents of 12 small islands off the coast near here are worried after noticing speedboats in the area, believed to be operated by human traffickers. The residents said the boats posed a risk to fishermen and villagers who frequently commute between the islands, particularly those returning home from work at night. A resident in Teluk Renjuna, who wished to be known as "Pak Din", said villagers were aware of the boat movements but preferred not to confront the alleged traffickers.

items.title: Trump administration targets seven Minnesota judges over ICE raid comments
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Justice Department asked a court Wednesday to punish federal judges in Minnesota who spoke to the media and criticised aggressive raids carried out in that state by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. On September 17, The New York Times published an article that quoted Judge Patrick Schiltz, the chief judge at Minnesota's federal district court during a series of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids last winter in Minneapolis, and six of the judge's colleagues on the bench. The Justice Department announced Wednesday it had filed a judicial misconduct complaint against Schiltz and the other six judges at a federal appeals court.

items.title: 'Excessive minimum wage increase could lead to cost shock for businesses' - ACCCIM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (Acccim) has cautioned that an excessive minimum wage adjustment could create a cost shock for businesses, particularly those operating on thin profit margins. Ng also highlighted the "ripple effect" of a minimum wage increase, whereby workers earning slightly above the minimum threshold could also seek higher wages. He said this could increase overall payroll costs as businesses adjusted wages across different levels to maintain existing wage differentials.

items.title: ECRL explained: How fast, how far and when will Malaysia’s new East Coast rail link open?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) could begin carrying passengers as early as mid-December, ahead of its original January 2027 launch target. Transport Minister Anthony Loke challenged MRL and CCCC in August 2026 to bring forward the start of ECRL operations to mid-December. How many passengers can the ECRL carry?

items.title: In Johor Bahru, firemen rescue 44 pupils and teachers in kindergarten trapped by flash flood
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Firemen managed to rescue 37 pupils and seven teachers who were earlier trapped in the Umiku Sayang Kindergarten and Nursery on Jalan Muhd Amin here after it was inundated by a flash floods today. Larkin Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Nakish Nekmat said that authorities received an distress call regarding the incident at 3.53pm. Following the call, a team of 10 firemen – equipped with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit – were dispatched to the scene that was located about 10 kilometres away.

items.title: Ex-EPF CEO proposes employers pay higher EPF contributions for low-wage workers while reducing contributions for high-income staff
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — To help lower-salary workers save up more money for their retirement through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), their employers could help put in more money towards their EPF savings, former EPF CEO Tan Sri Shahril Ridza Ridzuan said today. Shahril, currently Axiata Group Berhad’s chairman, noted that Malaysia currently has one of the highest contribution rates from employees and their employers for retirement savings in EPF. Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000).

items.title: Several areas in Johor Bahru hit by flash floods following heavy rain (VIDEO)
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Several areas in the Johor Bahru district and city were hit by flash floods following a heavy afternoon downpour. https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19Y6wverdL/?mibextid=wwXIfr The roads affected were Jalan Kolam Air, Jalan Ayer Molek, Jalan Yahya Awal, Jalan Pantai and Jalan Wong Ah Fook in the city. https://www.facebook.com/100093466671276/videos/himpunan-rakaman-video-keadaan-banjir-kilat-di-sekitar-pusat-bandaraya-johor-bah/1939811560728289/

items.title: EPF CEO outlines four priorities for Malaysia as Malaysians live longer, says all have role to play
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia now faces four priorities as Malaysians are expected to live longer lives, including shifting from just thinking about having money for retirement to having income for the remaining years, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) CEO said today. EPF CEO Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn noted that longevity is one of the biggest defining forces that will impact Malaysia, including its society and economy. “Income security, health, care, work, and community all shape how well people live longer lives,” the retirement savings fund’s CEO said in his closing remarks at the two-day ISWC 2026 here.

items.title: Fahmi asks MCMC to clarify Meta’s response on WhatsApp issues
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has asked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to issue a statement clarifying Meta’s response to issues involving hacked and deactivated WhatsApp accounts. However, he said he had yet to receive an update on discussions between MCMC and Meta on the matter. Meta had requested until 3 pm last Monday to submit its response to issues raised by MCMC concerning hacked and deactivated WhatsApp accounts.

items.title: Selangor allocates RM100,000 to help wives and children wronged in maintenance issues
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 30 — The Selangor state government has allocated RM100,000 for the implementation of the Selangor Rahmah Maintainence Assistance Programme 2026 to strengthen social protection and welfare for women and children who have been wronged due to syariah judgement debtors. Selangor Women’s Development and Community Welfare Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said that the temporary financial assistance is estimated to benefit up to 50 affected families while the law enforcement process is carried out. He said the one-off assistance was distributed according to the rates set by the Family Support Division (BSK) of the Selangor Syariah Judiciary Department (JAKESS) at RM2,000 for the wife and RM1,000 for each child.

items.title: Johan Setia reports highest unhealthy API level at 166, twenty areas in total experiencing bad air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Twenty areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest level at 166. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four other areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy air quality: Shah Alam (164), Klang (158), Petaling Jaya (155) and Banting (143). Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three were at a good level.

items.title: Sarawak hydrogen market viability still unproven, says analyst
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 30 — Putrajaya should think twice about extending incentives to Sarawak’s hydrogen sector when it has yet to prove that there are enough buyers willing to pay commercially viable prices, according to an analyst. He said the basic problem with hydrogen was not Sarawak’s ability to produce it, but whether anyone wanted to buy enough of it at a price that made the business sustainable. “You can build the plant and produce the hydrogen.

items.title: Flying this weekend? Malaysia Airlines urges KLIA passengers to arrive early amid Sepang F1 traffic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia Airlines advises passengers travelling from KL International Airport (KLIA) on Oct 2-4, 2026 to allow additional travel time to the airport, due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit. “Passengers are advised to arrive at KLIA at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights and two hours before the scheduled departure time for domestic flights to ensure a smooth process. “Malaysia Airlines said the check-in counters close 60 minutes before the scheduled departure time for both domestic and international flights,” it said in a post on X.

items.title: Immigration Dept denies social media claim that Myanmar teen was repatriated, says she remains in detention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Immigration Department today denied claims that a Myanmar teenage girl was among those repatriated to Myanmar yesterday, saying she remains in custody at an immigration detention depot. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks by the department found that the teenager was not involved in the September 29 repatriation programme, which saw Myanmar nationals transported home aboard Myanmar naval vessels. “Checks by the department confirmed that the individual remains detained at an Immigration depot and was not involved in the repatriation programme for Myanmar nationals via Myanmar military vessels yesterday,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Myanmar man gets 16 years’ prison for killing 80-year-old fruit seller in Taman OUG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A Myanmar man was sentenced to 16 years’ imprisonment by the High Court today after pleading guilty to causing the death of an elderly fruit seller at a house in Taman OUG, three years ago. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin handed down the sentence on Shofi Husson Fozo Rahman, 29, and ordered the accused to serve the prison term from the date of his arrest on Sept 26, 2023. “The accused behaved well while in prison.
